records.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). That calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so every instance created without an explicit `queued` will share the same stale timestamp. records.issue_text: `from_dict` does no type validation; a string integration_id passes key-name checking, causing the should_sync comparison to compare str vs int so loop protection is silently disabled for such payloads
records.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, the code returns `cls(**input_dict)` and only catches `(ValueError, TypeError)`; dataclass type annotations (`integration_id: int`) are not enforced at runtime, so `{"integration_id": "123", "source_name": "x"}` would successfully construct an `AssignmentSource` with a string `integration_id`. Then `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` does `if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id: return False`—a `str` vs `int` comparison will be `False`, silently bypassing the loop-prevention check for such payloads.
records.stripped_text: `from_dict` does no type validation; a string integration_id passes key-name checking, causing the should_sync comparison to compare str vs int so loop protection is silently disabled for such payloads
